title: Ravana and Maricha's warning
hook: the king of Lanka hears the news, makes a plan, and is talked out of it on the first try
tomorrow: Ravana and Maricha's warning, part two

segments.voice: Yesterday: Khara and Dushana, part two. Rama alone defeated their army and kept his promise, but Akampana escaped toward Lanka. Did you keep a hard promise? Day five hundred sixty-five.

Until now, the Ramayana has spoken of Ravana without showing him. Now the story crosses the sea, into his city. Akampana arrives in Lanka shaking, and tells the king of the rakshasas everything: Janasthana is empty, Khara and Dushana are dead, fourteen thousand lie on the field, and one man did it. Ravana's first response is rage. Who is this man? I'll burn him. And Akampana says: you can't beat him. But I know how you can hurt him.
screen: `ACROSS THE SEA, IN LANKA.` → `ONE MAN DID THIS.` → `I KNOW HOW TO HURT HIM.`

segments.voice: Akampana's idea is cold. Rama has a wife, Sita, and no woman in the world, he says, is her equal in beauty. Carry her off, and Rama will die of grief without a single arrow. Ravana likes it. He takes his chariot across the sea to the hermitage of an old acquaintance, Maricha. Remember that name. Maricha is the rakshasa Rama spared years ago, at Vishvamitra's sacrifice, hurling him out to sea alive. He's lived as a kind of hermit since. Ravana tells him the plan and asks for help. And Maricha says no. Who told you to do this, he asks. Whoever it was is your enemy pretending to be your friend. Rama is a sleeping lion. Don't go poke him. Go home, enjoy your wives, and let him live with his. And here's the surprise. Ravana listens. He turns around and goes home to Lanka. If the story stopped there, it would be a story about good advice taken. But someone else is on her way to Lanka. Shurpanakha arrives at Ravana's court, mutilated, and she doesn't plead. She scolds. What kind of king are you, she says, lost in pleasure while a man destroys your army and your frontier? You don't even know what's happening in your own lands. And then she describes Sita, at length. The warning that worked once is about to be overruled. Pride, stung in public, is harder to talk down.
screen: `TAKE HIS WIFE, AKAMPANA SAYS.` · `MARICHA: DON'T POKE THE LION.` · `RAVANA GOES HOME.` · `SHURPANAKHA SHAMES THE KING.` · then, large: `PRIDE STUNG IN PUBLIC.`

segments.voice: Sit and breathe evenly. Think of a piece of good advice you once took, when you calmed down and decided against something. Remember how it felt to let it go. Now think of a time your pride got stung, in front of others, and you wanted to prove something. Notice how different those two feelings are in the body. Let your breath slow, and rest in the first one. The bell holds the time.
Ravana and Maricha's warning. Maricha tells Ravana not to wake the sleeping lion, and Ravana listens, until Shurpanakha shames him.
Your line: Ravana and Maricha's warning. Today, if your pride gets stung, wait an hour before you decide anything. Day five hundred sixty-five.

howItsDone: Recitations of the Aranya Kanda that tell this part in full keep Maricha's first refusal, so listeners hear that Ravana was talked out of the plan once before Shurpanakha's scolding changed his mind.

fork.setup: you're Ravana. an old rakshasa tells you your plan comes from an enemy dressed as a friend. what do you do?
options: take the advice and go home.
fork.reveal: Ravana listens and goes home, the first time. then Shurpanakha arrives and shames him in public.

original.note: Sanskrit rāvaṇa: traditionally explained as 'the one who makes others cry out,' the king of the rakshasas in Lanka.

trapdoor: what you thought: Ravana decides to steal Sita the moment he hears of her.
what it means: he's talked out of it once, and changes his mind only after public shame.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 31 gives Akampana's plan and Maricha's first refusal; Aranya 32–34 Shurpanakha's rebuke to Ravana as a negligent king.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda 31 (Akampana's report and plan; Maricha's first warning)
Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda 32–34 (Shurpanakha in Lanka)
Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 30 (Maricha spared at Vishvamitra's sacrifice)

notes: Maricha's 'sleeping lion' image and 'enemy in a friend's guise' paraphrased from Aranya 31; confirm.
The explanation of Rāvaṇa ('one who makes others cry out', from ru, to roar/cry) is traditional, given in Uttara Kanda; confirm wording.
The hook's 'first time we're in his city' is a narrative claim: Ravana is mentioned earlier (Bala Kanda) but this is his first scene in Lanka; confirm.
